To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a dual-core 64-bit UltraSPARC IIIi microprocessor has been implemented in a 1.1 GHz 0.13-micron Cu process, and that (b) this processor offers an efficient performance/power trade-off for compute-dense applications.
a 1 MB integrated dual-core 64 bit processor with 1.6 GHz clock frequency can be designed in a 0.13 /spl mu /m Cu technology with 2.1 W total power consumption.
a dual-core UltraSPARC IIIi microprocessor with 1 MB of integrated L2 cache is implemented in 0.13/spl mu/m Cu process technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a high-performance, low power, low cost, dual core processor for server applications.
the design, implementation, and evaluation of a dual-core processor for dense server applications in a 0,13 /spl mu/ Cu process.
the development of an energy efficient, low-power processor architecture for the next generation of high-performance, high-density servers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of the dual-core processor is a significant step forward in the evolution of high-performance, low-power microprocessors.
the 0.13/mu m Cu process is a very promising process to be used for high performance processors.
the design of the 1.35 GHz UltraSPARC T2 processor was a success, and the design team is very happy to have contributed to the success of the UltraSPARC T1 processor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a processor core, previously fabricated in a 0,25 /spl mu/, Al process, is designed and fabricated in a 90 nm, low-k process.
we were able to achieve 1.2X higher performance and 1.6X higher power efficiency than a single core processor with the same area and power budget.
we have been able to achieve a 1.6x performance improvement over a single-core UltraSPARC T1 processor, while reducing power consumption by 50% and die size by 30%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dual-core UltraSPARC IV+ is the first dual-core processor to be implemented in a 90 nm process.
the dual-core design is not only feasible, but can also provide a performance/power ratio that is comparable or better than that of a single-core processor.
the 0.13/spl mu/m Cu process offers a significant improvement in power and performance over a 0.18/spl mu/m process, while providing a 2x increase in density and 3x reduction in leakage power.
